## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Visākhātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.13, also cited as Thī 13) is a short canonical poem preserved in the *Therīgāthā* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Collett 2014]. The verse is ascribed to an elder nun (*bhikkhunī*) named Visākhā, who is distinct from both the prominent lay benefactress Visākhā (Migāra's mother) and the male lay disciple Visākha [Collett 2014].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any curated or computed cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit literature [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus records six text-reuse alignments between the verse and its commentary in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0509a), where verses §0.3–1.4 of the root text correspond closely to commentary sections §226–227 [DharmaNexus].
